report_name: Allies Expose Chinese Hacking Contractor 'Integrity Technology Group'

threat_actors.name: Integrity Technology Group
threat_actors.description: A sanctioned, China-based for-profit hacking contractor that develops and deploys cyber capabilities for Chinese state-sponsored threat actors like Flax Typhoon. The U.S. Department of Justice seized domains and tools used by the group.
threat_actors.goals: Provide hacking tools and services for state-sponsored espionage campaigns targeting critical infrastructure, government, healthcare, and manufacturing sectors.

threat_actors.name: Flax Typhoon
threat_actors.description: A Chinese state-sponsored threat actor known for targeting critical infrastructure, government, and other sectors in Taiwan and other regions. It utilizes tools and services provided by contractors like Integrity Technology Group.

attack_patterns.name: Vulnerability Scanning
attack_patterns.description: Used the custom utility 'MicroScan' and other open-source tools to actively scan networks for specific vulnerabilities as part of the reconnaissance phase.

attack_patterns.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
attack_patterns.description: Gained initial access by exploiting cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerabilities in web applications.

attack_patterns.name: Password Spraying
attack_patterns.description: Used the 'EBurst' tool to conduct password spraying attacks against Microsoft 365 accounts to compromise credentials.

attack_patterns.name: Remote Email Collection
attack_patterns.description: Used the 'office-cli' command-line utility to exfiltrate emails from compromised Outlook 365 accounts.

malware.name: MicroScan
malware.description: A custom utility developed by Integrity Technology Group that contains over 1,300 penetration testing scripts used to scan networks for vulnerabilities.

malware.name: EBurst
malware.description: A custom tool developed by Integrity Technology Group used to conduct password spraying attacks against Microsoft 365 accounts.

malware.name: office-cli
malware.description: A command-line utility developed by Integrity Technology Group used to target and exfiltrate emails from compromised Outlook 365 accounts.

malware.name: FishHub
malware.description: A custom hacking tool developed and used by Integrity Technology Group, which was seized by the U.S. Department of Justice.

tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description: Used to interact with the Microsoft Graph API for email exfiltration after an account is compromised.

vulnerabilities.name: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
vulnerabilities.description: The advisory mentions the exploitation of cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerabilities in web applications for initial access.

identities.name: Microsoft
identities.description: Vendor of Microsoft 365, which was targeted by password spraying and email collection attacks.

identities.name: U.S. Department of Justice
identities.description: Announced the seizure of domains and hacking tools used by Integrity Technology Group as part of a coordinated government response.

indicators.name: ITG Tool 'office-cli' File Detection
indicators.x_netsecio_sigma_rule:
title: ITG Tool 'office-cli' File Creation
id: 7e8b9c0d-1a2b-4c5d-8e9f-0a1b2c3d4e5f
status: experimental
description: Detects the creation of the 'office-cli' tool used by Integrity Technology Group for email exfiltration.
references:
  - https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/uk-allies-threat-china-integrity/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-10
tags:
  - attack.t1114.002
level: high
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|endswith: '\office-cli'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the presence of the 'office-cli' tool on disk.

indicators.name: ITG Tool 'office-cli' Command Line Execution
indicators.pattern:
title: ITG Tool 'office-cli' Command Line Execution
id: 1a2b3c4d-5e6f-4a7b-8c9d-0e1f2a3b4c5d
status: experimental
description: Detects the execution of the 'office-cli' utility, a strong indicator of ITG activity for email exfiltration.
references:
  - https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/uk-allies-threat-china-integrity/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-10
tags:
  - attack.t1114.002
  - attack.collection
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\office-cli.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: 'office-cli'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the execution of the 'office-cli' utility used for email exfiltration from Outlook 365.

indicators.name: Potential M365 Password Spray Attack
indicators.pattern:
title: Potential M365 Password Spray Attack
id: 2b3c4d5e-6f7a-4b8c-9d0e-1f2a3b4c5d6e
status: experimental
description: Detects a high volume of failed Microsoft 365 login attempts from a single IP address, followed by a success, which is indicative of a password spray attack.
references:
  - https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/uk-allies-threat-china-integrity/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-10
tags:
  - attack.t1110.003
  - attack.credential_access
level: medium
logsource:
  product: m365
  service: audit.azuread
detection:
  selection_failed:
    Operation: 'UserLoginFailed'
  selection_success:
    Operation: 'UserLoggedIn'
  timeframe: 10m
  condition: selection_failed | count(User) > 10 by ClientIP and 1 of selection_success
indicators.description: Detects a high volume of failed Microsoft 365 login attempts from a single IP followed by a success, indicative of a password spray attack using a tool like EBurst.

indicators.name: Anomalous PowerShell Access to Microsoft Graph API
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous PowerShell Access to Microsoft Graph API
id: 3c4d5e6f-7a8b-4c9d-0e1f-2a3b4c5d6e7f
status: experimental
description: Detects PowerShell being used to interact with the Microsoft Graph API, which can be a sign of email exfiltration after an account compromise.
references:
  - https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/uk-allies-threat-china-integrity/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-10
tags:
  - attack.t1114.002
  - attack.collection
level: medium
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\powershell.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: 'graph.microsoft.com'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects PowerShell being used to interact with the Microsoft Graph API, a TTP associated with ITG for email exfiltration.
